formato: CourseGradingConfig.exam_script (apps/practice/conversa/exame.py, validar_guiao); carregar com manage.py carregar_exame_curso

perguntas.pergunta: Hello, {nome}. Welcome to your C1.1 speaking exam. Tell me about your work or your studies. What do you think really makes the difference in your field?
perguntas.simples: Tell me about your work or studies. What is most important in your field?

perguntas.pergunta: Looking back, what is one piece of advice you were given that changed your work or your studies? What would have happened without it?
perguntas.simples: What good advice did you get? How did it help you?

perguntas.pergunta: Where do you think your field is heading in the next ten years? And how sure are you about that?
perguntas.simples: How will your field change in ten years?

perguntas.pergunta: Now please talk for about one and a half minutes. A company with two hundred employees can offer one new benefit: health insurance for families, a crèche at the office, or one month of paid study leave a year. Choose two, compare them, and say which would make the bigger difference.
perguntas.simples: Three benefits: health insurance, a crèche, or study leave. Choose two, compare them, and choose one.

perguntas.pergunta: Thank you. What might the company regret if it chose the option you did not recommend?
perguntas.simples: What problems could the other option cause?

perguntas.pergunta: Some employees have no children and do not study. How would you make your choice feel fair to them?
perguntas.simples: How can the choice be fair for everyone?

notas: Ask one question at a time and wait. Do not correct, teach or give hints. If the student takes time to think, reformulates, corrects themselves or disagrees politely, continue normally.
If the student answers with one word or one short sentence, ask Could you say a bit more about that? once per question.
In Part 2, let the student talk for about one and a half minutes without interrupting. If they describe all three options or do not choose, ask And which would you choose, and why? once.
If the student does not work, adapt the questions to their studies, their family or their community.

In the situation, create the difficulty described in it once, and at least once ask for something the student should refuse or soften. The task ends only with a clear decision; if the student does not close it, ask So, what do we decide?
If the situation has two characters, play both and always say the name before each line.
After the situation, ask its discussion question. Give the first opposite view and wait; then the second and wait. This is Part 4 (about 3 minutes). Expect nuance, not only agreement or disagreement.

Use any language up to C1 unit 5, but not legal language like hereby, the future in the past like was to have been, fronting like Expensive it may be, mind you, that said, give or take, -ish, or so, or idioms like the ball is in your court.

tarefa.80-100: Developed, persuasive answers with a clear main point; chooses two of the three options, compares them, speculates and chooses with reasons; leads the situation to a clear decision, refusing or softening where needed; answers both counter-arguments with nuance.
tarefa.60-79: Developed answers, though not always persuasive; compares two options but speculates little; reaches a decision with some help; answers the counter-arguments, but without much nuance.
tarefa.40-59: Short or unfocused answers; talks about the options without choosing; the situation ends without a real decision; simple agreement or disagreement in Part 4.
tarefa.0-39: Answers few questions, or answers in Portuguese.

gramatica.80-100: A wide range of complex structures used naturally (cleft sentences, hedging, mixed conditionals, conditional and negative inversion, participle clauses, reporting passives); mistakes are rare and hard to notice.
gramatica.60-79: Uses several C1.1 structures, with some mistakes of form (for example There seem to be a, or the wrong subject after a participle clause), but the meaning is always clear.
gramatica.40-59: Mostly B2 structures; few or no C1.1 structures; mistakes sometimes make the meaning unclear.

vocabulario.80-100: Precise, varied vocabulary and collocations from C1 units 1-5 (persuasion, diplomacy, strategy, conflict, data); approximates numbers honestly; adapts the register to the situation.
vocabulario.60-79: Good range for the tasks, with some collocations; some imprecise words; paraphrases easily when a word is missing.
vocabulario.40-59: Limited range; general words instead of precise ones; repeats the same words.
vocabulario.0-39: Very few words, or many Portuguese words.

fluencia.80-100: Speaks fluently and almost effortlessly in long, organised turns; leads the decision task; only an abstract question makes them pause.
fluencia.60-79: Mostly fluent, with some pauses to find structures; follows rather than leads in the task.
fluencia.40-59: Short turns and frequent pauses; needs help to continue.

nao_baixa: asking the examiner to repeat or to explain a question
taking a moment to think before an abstract question
reformulating: What I mean is... or In other words...
correcting yourself with Sorry, I mean...
disagreeing with the examiner politely, or agreeing only in part
leaving one of the three options aside in Part 2
one isolated mistake when the structure is clearly C1
